bullets: Heat from the sun lifts the warm air, cooler air flows in, and clouds gather to bring rain
slides.heading: Weather and climate: heat on the move
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we follow heat on the move - the sun heats the land, warm air rises while cool air flows in, and clouds gather until rain falls - and we learn to tell today's weather from the climate.

bullets: Explain how the sun heats the land and sets the air moving
Describe how rising warm air, flowing cool air, clouds and rain link together
Tell weather apart from climate: one day versus the pattern over many years
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the goals aloud and tell the class: keep these in mind, because the exit ticket at the end will ask you to trace the heat chain and to explain the difference between weather and climate.

bullets: This morning felt freezing, so a pupil wonders whether the whole climate is changing
Can one single day tell us that, or do we need the pattern over many years?
slides.heading: One cold morning - has the climate changed?
slides.notes: Pose the puzzle without the verdict first: ask for a show of hands on whether one cold morning proves the climate is changing, take two or three answers without judging them, and say the weather-versus-climate idea in this lesson settles it.

bullets: Weather is what the air is doing today: sun, wind, clouds and rain
Climate is the pattern of weather over many years
The sun starts the chain: it heats the land, and the land warms the air above it
slides.heading: Weather is today, climate is the long pattern
slides.notes: Say this slowly, because it is the big idea of the whole lesson: Today's weather is not the climate: climate is the pattern of weather over many years, not one cold or hot day. Hold on to that difference while we watch the heat chain in the next three scenes.

bullets: The sun pours heat onto the land
The land warms the air sitting above it, and that warm air begins to rise
slides.heading: The sun heats the land
slides.notes: Narrate the scene as it plays: point to the sun's rays reaching the land, then watch the warmed air above the land start to lift - heat from the sun is what lifts the air.

bullets: The warm air rises high above the land
Cooler air flows in to take its place - that moving air is what we feel as wind
slides.heading: Warm air rises, cool air flows in
slides.notes: Follow the warm air climbing and the cooler air sliding in underneath it: name the moving air as wind, and stress that the inflow happens because the rising air leaves room behind.

bullets: High up, the risen warm air cools and gathers into clouds
The drops in the clouds grow heavy and fall back down as rain
slides.heading: Clouds gather, rain falls
slides.notes: Watch the cooled air gather into clouds overhead: as the drops grow heavy they fall as rain, completing the chain that began with the sun heating the land.

bullets: Start with the sun heating the land and warming the air above it
The warm air rises, cool air flows in as wind, and high up the air cools into clouds that drop rain
slides.heading: Worked example: follow the heat from land to rain
slides.notes: Talk through the chain slowly and name each step: sun heats the land first, then warm air rises while cool air flows in, and finally clouds gather and rain falls - one chain, three scenes.

bullets: Put the three scenes in order and say what happens at each step
Explain in one sentence how weather differs from climate
slides.heading: Your turn: put the heat chain in order
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes, then cold-call one pair on each part: press them to order the scenes correctly, to name wind as the in-flowing cool air, and to define climate as the pattern over many years.

bullets: On your own: trace the chain from the sun heating the land to rain falling
Say what climate means and why it is not the same as one day of weather
slides.heading: Exit ticket: show what you know
slides.notes: Collect these before anyone leaves and say: I am looking for the full chain - sun heats the land, warm air rises, cool air flows in, clouds gather, rain falls - and climate described as the pattern of weather over many years.
